about: Electoral votes by state for the 2024 and 2028 presidential elections: each state's House seats under the 2020 apportionment plus two, and three for the District of Columbia (U.S. Const. art. II, § 1; amend. XXIII). Maine and Nebraska award two electors statewide and one per congressional district; the game awards all of a state's electors to its statewide winner for now.
source: National Archives, 'Distribution of Electoral Votes' (2020 census apportionment), https://www.archives.gov/electoral-college/allocation
withoutHouseDelegationSource: National Archives, 'The Constitution: Amendments 11-27', https://www.archives.gov/founding-docs/amendments-11-27. Amend. XII: in a contingent election "the votes shall be taken by states, the representation from each state having one vote"; amend. XXIII, sec. 1: "The District constituting the seat of Government of the United States" appoints electors only, so it has electors and no state delegation in the House.
